claims.text: Simultaneous mechanical wear and corrosive exposure promotes a dynamic cycle of passive-film removal and reformation in high-entropy alloys.
The passive-film removal and reformation cycle governs resistance to combined wear and corrosion.
Mechanical wear removes the existing passive film and exposes fresh alloy surface.
The freshly exposed alloy surface rapidly oxidizes and forms a new passive film.
The newly formed oxide layer is protective.
Sufficiently rapid re-passivation mitigates mechanical wear.
The proposed initial alloy has a near-homogeneous distribution of multiple elements.
Multiple elements in the proposed alloy form stable, corrosion-resistant oxides upon exposure.
Repeated passive-film renewal limits overall degradation under simultaneous wear and corrosion.
The test alloy will have lower wear depth under simultaneous wear and corrosion than a matched variant with a less effective or absent re-passivation response.
The test alloy will have slower corrosion-pit growth under simultaneous wear and corrosion than the matched baseline variant.
Reducing the concentration of passivating elements produces a less effective re-passivation response and higher degradation under otherwise similar conditions.
The protective effect diminishes when passive-film removal by wear outpaces passive-film reformation.
The prediction should hold at moderate wear rates that allow effective passive-film reformation.
The prediction may fail under extreme wear or in environments where film-formation kinetics are too slow relative to film removal.
